view.rationale: Q2 revenue and licensing materially exceeded the pre-release setup, and the company raised FY revenue growth to 13-15% and lifted FY profitability growth targets. However, options/price action and the note’s positioning (“priced for perfection” after an ~9% pre-print rally and rich multiple) reduce the upside to an expectedly modest response rather than a strong rerating.

Despite a modest Q2 ARR/currency performance, management cut FY26 ARR and revenue and guided Q3 to further deceleration. Renewal rates fell (mid-80s vs high-80s) with gross margin declining and weakening UEM/EDR demand—worse than the note’s base/implicit hold-through scenario, implying downside pressure on the ARR bridge and multiple.

Q2 revenue missed the (already-demanding) expectations band and, more importantly, FY26 guidance was cut sharply (midpoint down ~17.5%) with cash-flow breakeven pushed to 2027 and margin guidance lowered—clear deterioration versus what the market was braced for. The only offset was better cash preservation and some diagnostics momentum (Anthem/CMS), which wasn’t enough to negate the guide reset.

Q1 revenue/EBITDA were roughly in line, but the company cut FY2027 revenue and—more importantly—adjusted EBITDA and free-cash-flow guidance, signaling weaker underlying earnings power. The SA contract acceleration is positive, yet chip-driven product timing and margin compression plus the back-half FCF downgrade drive a likely negative repricing versus the pre-release setup that centered on holding the FY27 EBITDA path.

Revenue and order momentum beat the note’s setup, but the printed margin weakness and still-limited backlog visibility (and the material weakness credibility/audit overhang) largely keep the outcome near base-case expectations. Full-year revenue guide was raised, yet margins remain pressured, offsetting upside.

Revenue was modestly above consensus, but the key watch item (backlog/book-to-bill) weakened vs the note’s base setup: consolidated backlog fell Y/Y with TTM book-to-bill still sub-1.0 (0.96) and Infrastructure remains weak (0.85). Full-year guidance was reaffirmed with no H2 uplift, so the incrementally negative backlog/profit-risk signal likely offsets the small revenue beat.

No meaningful revenue and EPS is mechanically impacted by warrant fair-value dynamics that the note already flagged. The main actionable item—cash and runway—came in roughly as expected (cash $23.9M and “beyond the interim”), but management still signaled funding likely needed before/for the full readout, limiting upside versus the note’s bull scenario.

Revenue was roughly in line with the pre-release framing of a stale/too-high consensus, but the company withdrew FY26 guidance (both sales and adj. EBITDA) and paused spending/expansion amid generic uncertainty and a strategic review—more negative than the note’s likely-cut scenario. The amended Hercules facility reduces near-term pressure but highlights worsening liquidity, which likely drives a downside reaction.

Q2 revenue missed consensus and, more importantly, Q2 Adj. EBITDA ($4.9M) is below the ~$5.5M “arithmetic floor” implied by the pre-print note. The key overhang (refinancing) did not come in as a relief item; instead, management lowered FY26 Adj. EBITDA guidance and flagged higher marketing spend and rising CAC, with softened trends into July—an earnings disappointment vs a turnaround setup.

Revenue of $218M vs the $221.9–$224.5M consensus range is essentially inline/slightly light, while the key launch narrative was better (266k Auvelity TRx; prescriber activation; new-to-brand script growth) but SG&A massively overshot the pre-Q expectation ($208.1M vs the ~$185–195M zone) even with guidance to plateau. With underlying cost pressure dominating, the net setup is neutral-to-slightly negative rather than a clear upside beat.

Q2 beat on sales/EPS and management raised FY26 sales growth to mid-single digits and widened the operating margin floor, but the quarter’s adj. op margin came in at 10.7% that was down sequentially vs prior comp and gross margin softened—while FCF fell sharply on working capital/tax timing. The guidance raise is partially offset by leverage uptick for FloWorks (1.8x on close) and the stock was already well-positioned heading in, so the net reaction skews slightly negative-to-neutral.

CECO delivered a stronger-than-soft-bar Q2 (record orders/backlog, margin expansion to mid-teens EBITDA) and—critically—raised FY26 low ends while synergy capture and FCF rebounded. Upside is only partially limited by the pre-release emphasis that the Q2 bar was low and the key risk was the back-half margin bridge; management addressed that with realized mid-teens margins and expanding synergy pace.

Despite better-than-feared capital actions/leverage and some pipeline strength, the Q2 continuing-ops revenue and adjusted EBITDA were materially worse than consensus, margins compressed sharply, and—most importantly—FY2026 guidance was cut meaningfully with the guidance now framed around discontinued operations. With the stock already needing a credible H2 EBITDA ramp, the lowered FY outlook drives a negative reaction versus expectations.

Reported TONMYA and total revenue materially beat the thin, revenue-only street setup (and were broadly aligned with the note’s bull/base script focus), with very strong prescription and refill growth. However, underlying cost structure deteriorated (higher R&D/SG&A) and cash runway language still points to dilution into early Q2’27, limiting upside versus what was already partly anticipated in the pre-release note.

Headline revenue/EPS and adjusted EBITDA beat the thin consensus, but the release also flagged a temporary Virginia buying surge and July/Aug seasonal slowdown plus a lower-than-expected Q1 gross margin driven by non-recurring FFL start-up costs. Underlying takeaway is strong GMV (+18.1%) and take rate expansion to 6.47% (from a pre-release focus on sub-6% risk), which should support a mildly positive tape despite demand normalization risk.

Because the quarterly financials were effectively pre-released (10-Q filed/summarized days before), the market is primarily pricing a capital-allocation/narrative outcome rather than a fresh earnings surprise. Reported GAAP loss was driven by non-cash ETH mark-to-market/impairment already flagged by the structure of the quarter; the only incremental concern is SG&A step-up from full ETH ops, slightly offset by buyback progress and treasury growth, keeping the net reaction modestly positive/neutral.

Q2 revenue and profitability beat the guidance and the note’s “guide drives the trade” framework, highlighted by a large EBITDA margin expansion and a raise in FY adjusted EBITDA. The main offset is Q4/Q3 margin guidance, which points to a decel/near-term gross margin dip (37.5–38.5%), plus the outlined revenue step-down from phasing out the low-margin resale stream.

JRSH beat the refreshed pre-release expectations on both revenue ($50.2M vs $48.86M) and EPS ($0.13 vs $0.09) with gross margin improving to 16.4% (above the 15–17% framing). Guidance for next quarter calls for slightly lower gross margin (14–15%) and revenue of ~$49–51M, which was broadly consistent with the scenario range; overall reaction is modestly positive given the stock had already run and the note flagged the revenue bar as near the top end.

Underlying results landed better than the note’s base (EPS concern didn’t materialize; adj. EBITDA and same-center growth supported the guided Q2 step-up). The key risk—Digital Health dilution/margins—was offset by ARR nearly doubling and imaging guidance was raised, despite a priced-for-raise setup; no meaningful negative came through.

Despite a +40% YoY adjusted EBITDA beat and maintained FY guidance, Q2 revenue missed by ~9% and RNG production growth decelerated and fell short of management’s expectations (high-50% utilization vs needed acceleration). With the stock already positioned mid-range and the note flagging H2 arithmetic/liquidity risk, the print likely dampens optimism rather than re-rates shares.

Headline Q2 revenue/EBITDA beat and full-year guidance was reiterated, but the quarter’s key call-out—student start growth collapsing to 1%—misses the note’s base-case expectation of a cleaner bridge, and CapEx guidance was raised sharply (growth investment drag risk). Offset by improved operating cash flow and liquidity, making the net reaction likely modest rather than strongly positive.

Reported revenue and especially adjusted EBITDA and margin expansion were stronger than the note’s base expectations for an in-line quarter. More importantly, FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance was raised (to $410–$420M and $85–$95M), and the 2027 exit trajectory was reinforced above $700M/$260M—supportive of the market’s core back-half ramp thesis. No credible negative signal (e.g., occupancy slip or margin deterioration) was introduced.

Revenue was roughly inline vs an upper-end consensus setup, and management reaffirmed FY26 revenue/adjusted EBITDA ex-Idaho. However, Q2 margin was slightly below prior year and the same-facility story showed case growth lagging (0.3%), plus commercial mix declined ~350 bps—offset by the clearer Idaho Falls deal terms and leverage step-down.

Fee-related revenue and FRE margin came in consistent with the pre-release setup, while fundraising exceeded the Q2 base and credit secondaries were a clearer onboarding signal. However, reported EPS/revenue (total) were not provided in the call facts, limiting the ability to mark a true headline beat; with the stock already near highs and priced for the positive FRE algorithm, the move is likely modest.

Revenue was below the published consensus but roughly in line with the note’s “real bar” (low-$20s). The bigger issue was underlying profitability deterioration (adjusted EBITDA sharply lower and traffic headwinds confirmed), which weakens the turnaround narrative; offset by debt refinancing completion and no dilution risk, plus an AI acquisition/rebrand that may be viewed as a strategic pivot.

Despite reaffirmed FY2026 EBITDA/sales guidance, Q2 results missed on revenue and (especially) adjusted EBITDA/margins, and cash fell sharply to ~$44M with net debt rising. The international decline and weaker absorption/freight headwinds point to underperformance versus what the note’s base case allowed, making the guidance hard to underwrite near term.

Revenue and gross margin beat the pre-release “financing quarter” framing, and FY2026 revenue guidance raised the low end. However, the key overhang wasn’t removed: cash/ramp language still implies future financing needs, and Q3 guide is only flat-to-modest with explicit manufacturing/order conservatism. Net: constructive ops and guide, but still a cash/recap risk limits upside reaction.

Q2 revenue beat the ~$27.29M consensus and gross margin hit a record 92% (helped by a tariff refund), while active accounts grew to 712 and management raised FY26 revenue guidance. However, FY26 revenue guide ($114–$117M) appears modest versus the pre-release expectation of a larger raise/upper guide (~$115–$118M), and GAAP EPS remains weak (net loss widened) which limits upside.

Underlying operating metrics improved (occupancy +240 bps; NOI margin +250 bps to 32.6%, with upside from transitions clearly showing through). Most importantly, the bridge loan was refinanced post-quarter (binary risk resolved in a favorable way), but management deferred formal 2027 normalized FFO guidance—reducing how much incremental info supports an outsized repricing versus the preview’s base case.

Revenue was broadly in line, and FY27 guidance was reaffirmed (no action vs the market’s base case). However, the quarter’s GAAP gross margin was weak (16.2% vs 18% prior; adjusted still only ~20.2% and FX headwind called out) plus cash flow was negative due to an inventory ramp—adding risk to the gross-margin step-up needed for the FY27 operating income bridge, even though tariff context was consistent with guidance.

Q2 Attruby net revenue and first-line share/gross-to-net commentary beat the pre-release trend/consensus bar, and management provided supportive clinical/real-world differentiation. However, EPS remains a material miss and the release adds major cash via the $1B preferred (funding optics) rather than proof of sustainable operating leverage, limiting upside versus the high bar priced into the stock.

Adjusted EBITDAX of $338M lands below the pre-release $370–410M range and below the note’s base case ($335–360M), with management also citing temporary takeaway constraints—so the core earnings power disappoints versus what the market had already framed around hedge/Brent cushions. Offsetting positives (synergies ahead of schedule; improved drilling efficiency; pipeline integration/maintenance assumptions) are real, but guidance for production and operating plan doesn’t clearly reverse the cash/FCF concern, and the company did not execute a buyback this quarter.

Despite strong unit shipments (5,100+), revenues fell short and gross margin turned negative. More importantly, customer deployment slipped 1–2 quarters and cash burn guidance was effectively worse (though a new ATM capacity was added). Net loss widened materially on warrant fair-value volatility, undermining the liquidity-and-ramp thesis versus what the note feared but also expected units/volume to show up without a major revenue shortfall.

Revenue missed consensus and, more importantly, management withdrew prior Q4 breakeven guidance and explicitly walked back the earlier Q4 revenue-growth stance. Gross margin contracted and cash declined, which compounds the pivot-risk; EPS slightly better than expected does not offset the guidance damage.

Headline revenue and, more importantly, the Commerce Media momentum and margin came in well above the preview’s “stall” thresholds (CMS run-rate >$125M; media margin expansion to 34%). Guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised, but the operating quality beat offsets the still-heavy microcap balance-sheet/going-concern overhang; the key downside is weak near-term cash/OCF.

Revenue and EBITDA were directionally in the preview’s “base/bear” zone, but the biggest incremental negative versus expectations was the company declining to provide any earnings guidance amid a worsening balance sheet/liquidity backdrop (low cash, maxed revolver) and margin compression. The negative catalyst is capital-structure uncertainty trumping the largely anticipated quarter weakness.

Cash came in at $47.1M (vs the note’s $43–47M base range) with an explicit “no planned raise before pivotal data,” and burn/R&D improved to broadly align with modeled expectations—so the balance-sheet risk looks contained. No evidence of a pivotal timeline slide or softer runway language that would drive a downside repricing.

Q2 headline revenue ($8.1M) and adjusted EPS ($0.23) beat the thin pre-release bar (the note even flagged a higher “real” EPS bar ~0.15). However, core system-wide sales ex-MRI were still described as pro forma (SWS down reported) and the stock was already up with the TrueBlue read-across priced in, limiting upside. No explicit guidance was provided, keeping reaction moderate-positive.

Q2 revenue slightly exceeded consensus, but adjusted EBITDA declined and gross margin fell (17.0% vs ~16.4% whisper), keeping the core earnings power in line-with/near the pre-set bear/base math. Headline net income beat was driven by one-offs (retention credit, tariff refund, swap), and the note already flagged governance/control and funding-plan risk as the main mover—no clear new guidance catalyst was provided in the release facts, keeping reaction modestly positive-to-neutral.

Headline revenue fell short of expectations and, more importantly, fiscal 2026 revenue guidance was cut while management attributed the weakness largely to wholesale and warned demand reaction to price increases was more negative than expected. EBITDA improved, but the margin boost was materially helped by a tariff refund, keeping underlying momentum less reassuring versus what the market was waiting to see (especially the H2 EBITDA cadence).

Q2 revenue and adjusted EPS beat consensus, and gross margin improved to near breakeven with improved fuel/PPA loss rates. More importantly, full-year revenue growth guidance was raised to 15–16% (above prior 13–15%), while the balance-sheet cash line remained consistent with the pre-release cash concerns (unrestricted cash ~$162M). Reaction expected to be modestly positive because the note already framed upside around margins/cash bridging and the stock has limited room versus that scenario.

Revenue and backlog substantially exceeded the pre-release scenario base expectations, with all-business-unit contribution and a higher-than-feared $42.5M backlog. Underlying profitability remains pressured (opex up and gross-margin inflection not stated), while EPS is largely mark-to-market driven and guidance was only reaffirmed (no clear upside sizing).

Revenue and adjusted-EPS expectations were broadly met, but the print shows slower underlying demand (SDC declines again; past-due backlog only modestly improving) even as margins expanded. With no full-year or FY27 guidance now (deferred to November) and the stock already priced high, the outcome reads more like ‘baseline’ than a clear upside reset.

Revenue and growth exceeded the pre-release base case (26.7M vs expected ~26.3M) and, importantly, adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 42% (above the guided mid/high-30s framework). That said, the equity offering was already priced into the setup and the market’s main uncertainty was capital-allocation/M&A commentary rather than headline results; limited excess upside beyond a strong beat. Guidance/margins were reaffirmed, reducing surprise risk.

Headline Q2 EBITDA and revenue were strong versus the pre-release framing, but underlying EBITDA was only ~$9M given ~$45M of favorable payer/prior-year development (i.e., the same settlement-driven risk the note flagged). More importantly, cash fell to $21M and at-risk membership declined (105k vs 116k) while Nebraska remains services-only through 2027—despite a FY EBITDA raise, the back-half liquidity/member glidepath leaves downside risk, tempering the reaction.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA landed essentially at/just above the low-single-digit and $150M midpoint expectations, with an FCF improvement that was directionally supportive. However, guidance was reaffirmed (not raised) and Q3 EBITDA ($180–220M) plus ongoing multiperiod margin compression risk leaves the $800M/H2 bridge heavily dependent on political + macro, so the market likely views the print as not resolving the core credibility issue.

Despite an EPS beat and higher full-year operating income guidance, the key issue was pre-committed to ARR decline and the release delivers a further sequential ARR drop to $824M plus a worse Q3 ARR outlook (~$812M). Gross margin fell again and non-core product declines continue, leaving little new underwriteable stabilization versus the note’s bear risks. Net: better P&L helps, but the ARR trajectory guidance dominates given the stock’s priced-for-perfection setup.

Underlying mix is better than the note’s mining-cash/recurring-lease concerns: data center recurring lease revenue rose sharply (+400% to $4.9M) and Engineering gross margin expanded materially (to >27%). However, GAAP EPS is deeply negative largely due to noncash mark-to-market, and the market signal to watch (postponement resolution / filings / any timeline reset) is unresolved in the provided facts, limiting upside and keeping the reaction near-median.

Q2 revenue of $107M missed consensus ($121.9M), and management still flagged only <10% of backlog converting (runway, but also suggests slow revenue monetization). While gross margin and adjusted EBITDA improved (12% GM; $4M adj. EBITDA) and backlog increased, the guidance raise to $525–575M remains below the $520M consensus anchor in the research note’s setup (and doesn’t resolve the note’s core H2 skepticism).

AAON smashed revenue and EPS versus consensus and raised FY revenue growth, but the release simultaneously delivered a gross-margin miss, margin guidance cut (~200 bps), and a backdrop of pressured backlog/bookings. With the note already flagging the two-sided nature (margin down/backlog softer) and the stock not obviously priced for perfection into the print, the net reaction is near-median slightly positive rather than sharply higher.

Q2 revenue missed expectations and underlying PRS/US dynamics stayed weak, while the company withdrew full-year revenue guidance (more negative vs the already cautious base case of a trim). Although gross margin improved on tariff refund/charges and gross loss is affected by higher interest expense, the combination of weaker-than-needed revenue run-rate plus guidance reset/cost details still unfinalized points to another downside repricing.

Headline revenue fell short of the loose consensus/market anchor and the adjusted EBITDA margin slipped, though client flows were strong. With the strategic review explicitly unchanged (“nothing further to report”), the market’s M&A-deal expectations provided limited upside; the cost/underlying margin pressure and the Asian fund unwinding add risk to the forward earnings power narrative.

Headline deal-driven backdrop made the setup cautionary, but the quarter itself landed better: Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss was at the better end of the guided range and Q2 revenue rose to $5.0M vs ~$1.95M consensus in the note (reframing expectations toward deal-quarter economics). Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance was held in the same range, and management reiterated no structural increase in cash burn, limiting downside. With the stock already having moved on deal news and the largest uncertainties being deal sizing/disclosure timing, reaction is modestly positive rather than a full beat-and-raise rerating.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat the top/end of guidance (margin expansion) and FY26 guidance was raised with higher EBITDA and EPS, but the stock trades the operating narrative and expects an in-line-to-modestly-better print; the biggest structural upside (registrations/Health+) was not clearly above the note’s bull/base thresholds, and Q3 embeds a timing shift with nonrecurring marketing optimization costs. Net: modest positive-to-muted reaction given the pre-priced setup and “beat-and-raise but maybe sell the news” pattern.

Q2 revenue landed in/near the practical consensus band and FY guidance was reaffirmed (no upside revision vs the note’s base). The key beat was adj. EBITDA exceeding the top end of guidance on record EBITDA/unit and margin expansion despite unit-growth headwinds; the offset was commentary pointing to conversion/macro-driven unit drag and higher no-reserve mix pressuring cost of revenue.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA came in far above the pre-release setup, and FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised (midpoint modestly above the $90M consensus midpoint). Despite a large GAAP noncash warrant hit and some cost pressure/labor shortages, the operating improvements (and very strong bookings/backlog metrics) and raised guide likely dominate, implying a meaningfully positive move versus typical base rates.

Headline revenue came slightly above the $99.65M expectation, and corporate cost discipline was better than what the base scenario assumed. However, the restaurant segment delivered a larger-than-expected impairment ($45M vs $1M prior year) and management explicitly flagged earnings variability from SpaceX mark-to-market—offsetting positives from liquidity and sports momentum. Guidance/action didn’t materially reframe the restaurant monetization path, keeping the reaction near-median.

Q2 revenue of $31.5M is below the ~$34M consensus implied in the note, but management reaffirmed the FY2026 $150–$200M range. The pro-forma financing/capex posture stays heavy and OpEx rose, offsetting government award positives; overall this fits the note’s base/bear mix rather than a clear beat-and-raise.

Q2 beat the high end of guidance on net income/adj. EBITDA and came in near the $51M guided ceiling, but the core thesis datapoints underwhelmed versus the note: digital subs fell to 760k (below the ~780k stabilizing/bull threshold) and gross margin declined, with Q3 calling for further margin contraction (42–45%). Guidance itself was maintained, so upside is capped by deterioration in the subscriber/margin trajectory despite improved profitability and added retail footprint.

Q2 revenue landed essentially in-line with the pre-release base case, while EPS beat meaningfully largely on profitability. The key item was guidance: FY26 revenue was tightened (midpoint essentially inline/slightly below the note’s consensus range), but FY26 adj. EBITDA midpoint was raised with ~100 bps margin expansion; that combination should be modestly supportive versus a priced-for-decline setup. However, RPO/deferred declines remain steep (RPO down 18%, deferred down 12%), so the bear trigger was not averted on the leading indicators.

Revenue and the Truth API commercial progress look better than the note’s modeled setup, but the core market driver—the near-term convertible-note repayment path—remains unresolved (cash largely encumberable; only partial liquidity), and crypto mark language remains a major swing factor. Net effect is a modestly negative reaction versus a note that already framed the balance-sheet/convertibility risk as the main issue.

Q2 revenue and ATS growth were strong versus the note’s base-case build, but management guided to a sequential Q2→Q3 ATS revenue decline and explicitly said Q2 was exceptional/unlikely to repeat—an outcome the note flagged as the key bear signal. Underlying margin did not deteriorate (ATS profit up), but the deceleration/guidance drives a negative skew.

DSP delivered a headline revenue beat (+34% YoY; modestly above the high end of guidance) and the key CTV/Direct Access momentum sounded strong (80%+ penetration; outcomes and IRIS progress). However, contribution ex-TAC came in just shy of the high end, and management reiterated a TVision drag on margins (bigger in Q3), keeping quality-of-growth risk front and center despite the raised Q3 guide.

Revenue was modestly below the (thin/stale) consensus, while losses widened and restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margin contracted vs a year ago despite sequential improvement. However, CPG momentum appears stronger (341% sequential growth, nearly 2,000 doors) and GEN raised the 12-month CPG run-rate, partially offsetting the weaker restaurant profitability; full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised.

Reported Q2 revenue ($18.5M) lands exactly at the company’s own pre-announced floor and below the “effective” $19–20M whisper flagged in the note; however, the call also delivered better mix (49% GM) and a record positive adj. EBITDA ($1.0M) while fully reiterating FY guidance ($85–90M revenue, >$5M adj. EBITDA) and providing high H2 visibility (~60% of revenue). Net result is a credibility/positioning check without a clear upside beyond what the note’s base case contemplated.

Revenue roughly matches the note’s ~24.5M base vs the single-broker ~$26.5M expectation, but the release emphasizes large one-time incentives/professional services and constrained Monovate card issuance (Lithuania inspection). The only meaningful upside is Monovate’s stronger-than-prior-year processing momentum, yet gating issues and cash burn keep the setup more neutral than a clear beat-and-raise story.

Because guidance has been withdrawn and the strategic review/sale process was already the central pre-release framework (including going-concern risk), the market should largely trade liquidity/covenants rather than a headline beat. Reported subscriber attach-rate improvement and record-like subscription engagement are incremental positives, but management provided no margin/sell-through/2H color—so the net reaction is close to neutral-to-slightly positive.

Q2 delivered a clean revenue/ subscriber upside and raised FY26 revenue guidance above expectations, but adjusted EBITDA and gross margin remained under pressure and margins are guided structurally lower. With the stock already rallied/positioned for an H2 bridge, the raise helps but deteriorating profitability and negative FCF temper the upside.

Underlying fundamentals in Q2 were broadly as expected for a pre-inflection, pre-revenue name, but management increased (worsened) second-half cash burn guidance to ~$8M/quarter from ~ $6M, citing regulatory/launch costs—an incremental negative vs the note’s base/bull runway assumptions. Additionally, RUO kit revenue was very small ($21K, ex-U.S.), and the July additional-information letter plus resubmission steps further heighten FDA/timeline uncertainty relative to the market’s focus on a smooth de novo path.

Q2 headline losses worsened materially (net loss and negative adj. EBITDA; cash flow swung sharply negative) while the release also delivered limited upside to the core Q2 watchpoints (Merom recovery proof point and margin stabilization). Positives like higher accredited capacity and a lowered Turtle Creek cost/earlier 2028 COD help, but the liquidity deterioration and ongoing margin/cash pressure dominate, making the outcome closer to the note’s bear/base mix than a clear beat-and-raise.

Revenue beat is driven largely by non-product (grant/collaboration) lines that were already the core bull case in the note, and the EPS comparison is contaminated by sizable investment gains and a tax benefit. However, product gross margin improved to 14% and management raised expectations via saying 2H results will exceed the full-year $52–60M guidance threshold—an incremental positive versus the note’s guidance/credibility focus.

Revenue roughly aligns with the stale ~$103M expectation, but underlying fundamentals deteriorated: gross margin fell to 29.5% (still down sharply) and adjusted EBITDA collapsed, while cash flow swung materially negative and volumes declined. Importantly, no FY guidance was reinstated (guidance remains an overhang per the note), and volume/margin and liquidity signals are worse than the base case framing.

Headline EPS was helped by a positive adjusted profit, but underlying operating metrics and—more importantly—guidance were cut materially (FY revenue/adj. EPS). India timing is pushed to H1’27 and recruiting/leadership are flagged as below needs, offsetting strong Prism.io device/scans progress.

Revenue landed within prior guide and the setup expected a modest beat at most; the bigger issue is Q3 gross margin guidance stepping down (non-GAAP below the top-end the market wanted) alongside worsened free cash flow. Contract/backlog strength is supportive but partially offset by cash/margin concern and diluted narrative around Neutron timing being tighter.

Q2 revenue came modestly above the low-end of the note, but adjusted EBITDA and (implied) EPS underperformed as higher fuel/driver costs hit—i.e., the cost story did not fully confirm the margin recovery. The release does, however, show sequential OR improvement (June 95.7%) and a second-half framework with OR ~97% and EBITDA margin 8–9%, which limits downside versus the note’s base/bear setup and supports only a neutral-to-slightly positive reaction.

Revenue and profitability beat materially (adjusted EBITDA $5.5M above the high end; gross margin 39.3% vs ~38% implied by the guide), while Q2 revenue guidance is maintained and backlog increased. Negative risk remains from tape supply constraint and a lower Q2 adjusted EBITDA guide, but the beat-and-raise is driven by operating execution rather than one-time items, making the net reaction mildly positive versus expectations.

Q2 revenue beat the already-approximate stub estimate, and—more importantly—first-ever formal guidance plus a strong Q3 range ($87–$93M) implies a materially faster consolidation/trajectory than the note’s base/bear framing. The stock is likely to respond positively given high guidance uncertainty and no clear underlying margin deterioration (adj. EBITDA loss narrowed).

Despite a (headline) Q2 revenue record, the key credit metric worsened to ~52% charge-offs and EPS fell to ~$0.33; more importantly, FY26 guidance was cut sharply (adj. EPS to $1.34–$1.51 vs prior $1.76–$1.84), driven by line-of-credit and system migration delays—effectively breaking the prior math needed for the back-half of the year.

Q2 revenue landed at the high end and adjusted EBITDA loss was within the guided range, while management reaffirmed FY revenue $128–138M and adjusted EBITDA loss $25–30M. The key incremental positive vs the note’s setup is stronger-than-needed momentum in private charter (record Q2, nearly doubled first-half) and a Q3 guide that tightens losses faster than a base-case would imply, with no evidence of a near-term equity raise. Delisting/risk-mitigation remains a headline overhang, keeping the reaction modestly positive rather than strong.

Underlying results largely match the note’s base case (~$100M revenue and ~$0.20 adj EPS) with margins explicitly attributed to mix from CUBRA. More importantly, FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance is reaffirmed (no bear-case detonation) and demand/progress metrics (business payments growth, supplier network) look better than the feared deceleration setup, supporting a modestly positive tape reaction.

Q2 headline revenue/Ebitda beat the high end, but the key is the guidance action: FY2026 revenue was cut to $730–750M (below the $760–790M range in the note) and Q3 guide implies weaker demand (revenue -/EBITDA margin down). Record GSV per client and take-rate strength are offset by falling active clients and faster-than-expected erosion of low-value work.

Q2 revenue and margins beat/track expectations with strong adjusted EBITDA and gross margin expansion, but the FY2026 revenue guide was trimmed (top end lowered) due to a more conservative airway outlook and some Medicare order timing pushed into Q3. With the market already primed for a softer Q2, the key new negative is the guidance cut tied to Airway/flow-through timing, which likely drives a muted-to-negative reaction despite the upside in profitability metrics.

Q2 delivered better-than-expected revenue (~$31.2M vs ~$29.7M) and a clear Adjusted EBITDA beat (~$7.0M vs ~$3.5M LY; note expected ~sub-$6M/EBITDA framing). Licensing growth returned (+~2% reported; ex-Byborg held back only slightly due to a China step-down) while HB comp momentum stayed strong (seventh straight double-digit comp). Debt deleveraging and the repurchase at $1.05 also support sentiment; no guidance action/new explicit framework was cited, so the upside is capped versus a bull-case guide/DEleveraging “hard number” surprise.

No pre-release expectations were provided, so surprises are inferred from direction of fundamentals. The quarter shows sharp revenue decline and worse adjusted EBITDA/cash burn, only partially offset by a key regulatory approval and reaffirmed launch timing.

The key yardstick in the note—Q2 TTV—came in weak ($169M) versus what the bull/base scenarios implied would be needed to sustain the unchanged ~$2.5B exit target (math requires ~$2.1B in 2H). Management also provided no 2027 guidance and pushed monetization/outcomes further toward late 2026/activations, keeping the growth credibility risk elevated. Headline GAAP EPS was artificially boosted by Transchem warrant remeasurement, so it doesn’t offset the operating underperformance.

Q2 revenue landed essentially in line, but adjusted EBITDA beat the high end of guidance and gross margin improved to ~26% despite higher marketing spend. The key negative was Q3’s constant-currency revenue guide (0.7%–3.3%) and EBITDA ($0–$5M), which is weaker than the note’s acceleration/base setup, plus Japan’s continued constant-currency decline remains the weak spot.

Headline EPS is sharply pressured by a large P3 CM-related pretax charge, which was a core overhang in the guidance math. Guidance is lowered for NSR growth and FY EPS/NSR at the midpoint, even as EBITDA margin targets are improved and backlog/book-to-burn remain strong—creating a mixed setup, but with downside control driven by the reduced earnings/cash outlook versus what the note anticipated.

Q2 revenue and EBITDA landed at the high end, and management raised FY revenue growth to 3–5% (incrementally above the pre-release base). However, gross margin guidance was cut 100 bps to 57–59% on unfavorable mix (more CMT, higher China), and cash remained tight (only $6.5M on hand; continued burn). Net effect is modestly positive but tempered by margin and liquidity risk.

Despite a modestly strong EPS/revenue print, the pre-release note expected a “quiet quarter” with losses and emphasized that Q3 headline was secondary. The real uplift was a guidance raise for FY26 adj. EBITDA ($15M vs ~$14M) and stronger-than-feared liquidity/cash trajectory, but EBITDA and operating cash-generation run-rate in Q3 was weak and management explicitly framed Q4 as an EBITDA-usage quarter—limiting upside.

Q2 revenue ($70.7M) came in about where the note expected (at/near the guidance floor vs depressed consensus), while management reiterated FY26 revenue ($350–365M) and EBITDA ($80–100M). Positives were record Vevye and AIHESO demand/pricing and high GM in Q2, but downside risk remains from the explicitly “lighter than expected” first-half timing and negative Q2 adjusted EBITDA, limiting upside reaction. Options implied a modest absolute move with downside skew, consistent with a neutral-to-slightly positive read.

Revenue was fully inline, but EPS/underlying loss came in worse than the pre-release framework (EPS miss) with R&D-driven margin deterioration and no partnering escalation. Offsetting positives were real restarts/uptick in R&D and stronger INVINCIBLE-4 Cohort A pCR (per the note’s direction), but the cash/runway math still looks constrained and partnering remains unresolved, keeping reaction near the base/neutral range.

Q3 delivered above-consensus revenue and a clearer EPS beat, while guiding fiscal 2026 organic growth to 9–10% (at/above the already-high bar) and confirming AOI/EPS growth ranges. Importantly for this setup, the Nexus scope expansion and ramp commentary were more constructive than a base/in-line quarter framework, and margin/international strength plus new-business wins reduce the feared timing-slip risk.

Despite a solid earnings beat on adj. EPS and record margins, underlying Q3 revenue was slightly weak and FY26 revenue guidance was cut (partly protests/materials) while FY27 growth is kept low (0–1%) with a larger-than-previous NASA headwind. The raise in EBITDA/EPS and better leverage are positives, but the guidance mix (lower top line vs held/raised earnings) plus narrative-driven Savannah River terms limits upside; reaction likely modestly negative/neutral.

Operationally, the print supports the core “timing reversal” thesis: adj. EBITDA rose to $9.8M (above the $9M level that mattered) with expanding margin, and orders/backlog were strong. However, EPS missed and liquidity remains thin, while management’s H2 strength is more “reassuring” than a clear incremental raise versus what was already modeled, keeping the net reaction modestly negative-to-neutral.

Core overhangs from the note were reiterated: FORTIFI-HN01 remains on track for substantial enrollment by year-end enabling a mid-2027 interim/possible accelerated approval, and cash/runway was reaffirmed (~$497M into 1H 2029). Operating expense growth guidance increases, but that was already the primary expectation (no explicit enrollment slip or interim delay), so the setup fits the note’s base/non-event profile.

Headline EPS beat was largely driven by an explicitly nonrecurring $100m IEEPA tariff refund; underlying EPS (after excluding the benefit) is closer to inline vs expectations. More importantly, the FY27 framework is mixed: EPS guide is slightly above consensus, but GMPD profit is guided down to a protracted/low-end range and FCF guidance drops materially with higher CapEx—on a stock already priced for strong execution and at/near highs—driving a likely negative reaction.

Revenue of $5.2M missed the ~$6.07M consensus and also breaks the note’s sequential-growth narrative (Q2 < $5.6M Q1). Offsetting positives were expanding gross margin (62%) and improved opex, but management’s H2/ARR conversion framing still implies most of the $13.1M contracted ARR lands in 2027, leaving the market’s key ask (H2 ramp toward implied ~$7.2M/quarter) less validated. Pro forma cash looks fine ($36.8M), limiting downside versus a going-concern fear.

Revenue and profitability were better than the note implied via the absence of GAC start-up costs (Adj. EBITDA +$5.8M vs ~$3.7M expectation). However, management reaffirmed FY26 and, crucially, did not commit to the GAC decision (potentially pushing into 2026/2027 with large $40–60M conversion costs), which is a credibility/liquidity overhang given the note’s no-slack math.

Q2 revenue came in ahead of consensus/base expectations and adjusted EBITDA loss improved substantially with gross margin expanding to ~57%. More importantly, full-year guidance low end was lifted to $68M-$70M while still excluding AVCAD, implying a less fragile 2H bridge than the note feared; near-term demand commentary (state/local) and NearLab device ramp supported the upside.

Headline revenue beat consensus, but management attributed the upside to a private-cloud one-time timing item and kept FY guidance unchanged; importantly, non-GAAP gross margin declined and FCF remained negative. AMD deal is a clear positive, but with margin pressure and an H2 revenue step-down narrative still unresolved, the setup is roughly neutral-to-slightly positive versus the note’s expectations.

Q2 headline growth looked broadly in line with the note, but the company delivered a record Adj. EBITDA and record utilization, plus raised FY26 Adj. EBITDA guidance to $103–108M (above the note’s mechanical bar). The key negative is that reported EPS/net income lagged expectations due to heavy transaction costs—offset by solid adjusted EPS and unchanged legacy guidance framing.

The quarter shows modestly higher revenue and confirms progress (five Stage 3 customers; multiple foundry runs), but the key negative vs the note’s bull/bear split is the widened loss and ongoing pre-commercial burn/opex scale-up, with the second material supply agreement still only “being negotiated” (no signed execution) and no sign of acceleration beyond what the note treated as base/on-track.

Underlying results look meaningfully better than the pre-release bar (notably gross margin +51.1% vs the ~48% needed for consensus EPS, and Adj. EBITDA inflecting positive). However, management also guided that 2H revenue may be choppier and FY revenue was narrowed (not raised), keeping the covenant/liquidity risk narrative in play—so the reaction is only modestly positive versus the downside tail implied by the going-concern setup.

TTEC missed on both revenue ($455M vs ~$478M) and the key EBITDA/leverage line (adj. EBITDA $39M vs ~$50–52M; net leverage 3.85x). Guidance for Engage was cut (midpoint revenue now -8% YoY and EBITDA margin 10.1% vs 10.6%), and management initiated a Digital strategic alternatives process with slower/smaller deal flow—incremental downside beyond what the note’s base case contemplated. Covenant flexibility and lower net debt are positives but don’t offset the underlying profitability/guide deterioration.

Q3 EBITDA and margin beat the key bar (~$79–80M and ~12.0%), and revenue/lb rose YoY as hoped. Guidance was raised for FY26 FCF and EBITDA tightened slightly upward vs the Street midpoint, but the EBITDA outlook implies Q4 is below the prior top-end range and management flagged a quadrant-4 drag that may keep pressure on volume/demand optics. Overall likely modestly positive given the stock was already positioned around an EBITDA recovery narrative.

Q2 undershot consensus revenue and delivered further margin deterioration with continued biologics/Amnio softness, while management cut FY26 revenue guidance again (to $99–103M) vs the note’s expectation that $101–105M would likely be reaffirmed or at most narrowed. With liquidity tightening (revolver ~ $0.7M) and no positive quantified HEMOBLAST ramp in Q2, the stock likely reacts negatively despite a largely expected low-revenue/margin backdrop.

Q2 revenue landed at the top end of guidance and EPS exceeded the top end, but the pre-print explicitly framed the likely outcome as “fine” with base-case largely priced in. The main incremental positives were (1) raising FY sales/EPS above the note’s base framing and (2) continued margin expansion, partially offset by the call’s Q3 electronics deceleration and an implied near-term momentum slowdown.

MG reported a clear EBITDA/margin beat and raised FY26 revenue and adj. EBITDA above the prior range and above what the note’s base case contemplated, with strong growth end markets offsetting weak Oil & Gas. The guidance raise is the key swing factor and should drive a modestly positive reaction despite the crude-linked headwind being known.

Revenue of $5.6M is essentially in the note’s low-to-mid $5.4–5.6M “whisper” range, and retention improved to 94% (an operational positive). However, gross margin fell to 73% vs 74% trough and adjusted EBITDA declined to $0.6M with no indication of an inflection in the near term beyond cost actions to restore margins later—offsetting the subscription/ARR progress for the stock.

Q2 adjusted EBITDA ($122.1M) was slightly ahead of consensus with strong RevPAR (+8.2% YoY) and clear labor/margin improvement, but guidance was only a reaffirmation and management explicitly noted occupancy growth is slower than anticipated—plus the implied lower full-year occupancy puts pressure on the higher H2 bridge expectations from the note. Net: modestly positive/near-median reaction.

Revenue came in essentially at the modeled base case (~$2.0M) and the key operational funnel metric improved (prior-auth approval rate up to 31% YTD; ordering-account revenue strong). EPS optics are muted by the pre-flagged stock-comp charge, and while gross margin expanded vs last year, it fell short of the preview’s expectation (85.9% vs ~86–87%). Overall reaction should be modestly positive/neutral given the lack of a clear beat vs setup and no decisive upside to the conversion path timeline.

Underlying profitability was better than expected (HE and total adj. EBITDA beat), but the quarter’s reported revenue and EPS were far worse because the rail contract exit adjustments and unusual P&L dominated. Guidance was maintained (no clean rail-loss narrowing), and the company flagged cash flow weakness (adj. FCF −$9M) plus continued Rail losses—factors likely to cap the upside despite the operating EBITDA beat.

Quarterly revenue was slightly below consensus while adj. EBITDA/margins deteriorated more than expected. The key driver is the FY guide cut (revenue and particularly EBITDA) tied to weaker demand and delayed acquisition revenue plus a major commercial segment decline—more negative than the pre-release bear/base mix despite the cheap multiple and prior stock weakness.

Q2 revenue and profitability largely met the note’s base case (near guide midpoint revenue; margins back to low-double-digit). The key incremental positive is guidance-linked deleveraging/financing (equity rights raising de-levering with near-term leverage reduction plus higher WolfPack synergy target), which offsets a mildly mixed setup from PIK reliance. Q3 revenue midpoint (~$182M) is constructive vs flat expectations, but not a dramatic upside blow.

Q2 revenue and—especially—adj. EBITDA missed the note’s base assumptions materially, with turnarounds down >50% and fixed-cost deleveraging driving margins lower. While the company reaffirmed full-year guidance, it also guided toward the lower half and disclosed only modest H2 cost-benefit timing alongside slightly negative operating cash flow, increasing downside risk to the EBITDA bridge.

Staking-led fundamentals largely matched the note’s modeled step-up (revenue jump; Gram holdings and operating income turning positive), so there’s limited upside vs what was already expected. However, the note’s key caution—sustainability of the 16%+ staking yield—was echoed by management (17% annualized and explicitly non-guaranteed), and the press/print includes sizable non-cash charges (Kingsway/stock comp), keeping the market reaction closer to neutral despite a strong headline fair value swing.

Q2 underlying performance was strong (CFS organic +8.3%, margin ~25.8% with only partial tariff relief), but the big swing factor from the note—standalone post-spin FY26 EPS basis and the H2 margin path—looks less favorable: full-year adjusted EPS guide is $6.73–$6.89 vs the note’s ~CFS-centric ~mid/high-$6.7s bull/base framework, and management guided higher incremental H2 inflation/margin pressure ($10–$15m) with pricing not material until Q4. Net effect is a modestly positive/near-median reaction rather than a strong beat-and-raise given guidance-basis reset risk.

Despite strong orders/backlog (Gearing/Industrial Solutions both growing and book-to-bill 1.5x), the quarter’s consolidated revenue came in well below the ~$34M consensus setup in the note, and management still declined to reinstate guidance until the Abilene wind-down completes in Q3. Industrial Solutions also guided to margin normalization lower going forward, capping upside and supporting a modestly negative/neutral stock reaction.

Pre-release framing flagged litigation/undertaking risk and ongoing same-store weakness, but the call reports EBITDA down YoY and gross margin pressure with sales down ~6% and Vegas/Florida down ~10–11%—worse underlying momentum than the note’s base/bull (which leaned on cost discipline offsetting revenue decline). No clear guidance shift was provided, but the deteriorating margin/demand tone is a negative for a name already priced for tails.

Underlying adjusted EBITDA beat the note’s ~$56–58M setup (reported $60.7M). However, management tightened the FY adjusted EBITDA range only slightly in the middle (midpoint reiterated at $245M) while raising capex guidance—so the main upside is execution/quality (Rockies/Mid-Con growth, added Williston connects) rather than a clear step-up in the credible H2 ramp that the market feared could break. Buyback was small, but leverage and Double E timing were maintained.

The release broadly matches the pre-read base case on the key driver (hedge losses ~mid-$60 range) and supports the capital-front-loading / lower 2H capex setup. LOE is still below guide (good) and EBITDAX/FCF grew sequentially, but there is no clear evidence of an upside guidance shift or a materially better-than-modeled hedge outcome versus what the note already warned about. With the stock having already improved materially into the print, the setup points to a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Clinically, multiple Phase 2/3 enrollment and MRD signals were stronger than the market baseline (faster enrollment, better MRD/ctDNA, no new safety signals). However, the cash position is only $6.9M and management explicitly flags the need for additional capital to execute Phase 3, reinforcing dilution/solvency overhang—an area emphasized in the pre-release note—so the net setup is modestly negative rather than a clean re-rate.

Headline results turned sharply positive (net income and adjusted EBITDA swung to profit) with both biofuel and chemical gross profit improving and utilization rising. The pre-release note stressed cash/runway and FY26 positive EBITDA/guidance and warned hedging/derivative marks could still weigh on headlines; FF instead reported meaningful gross-profit improvement and held substantial cash with no revolver borrowings, suggesting fewer liquidity/margin concerns than feared, though EPS/revenue vs consensus can’t be quantified from the note.

Q2 revenue ($7.9M) and EPS were far below the pre-release consensus, and—more importantly—FY2026 revenue guidance was cut sharply to $60–$75M (well below both consensus and the already-strained $125M guide). The miss was driven largely by much weaker realized antimony pricing and gross margin collapse (7%), not timing relief, so the market reaction is strongly negative versus what was already expected.

INUV’s revenue was essentially in line with the (already dire) $7.76M consensus, but the loss was worse and gross margin deteriorated further (44% vs ~mid-40s expectation implied by the pivot). More importantly, liquidity remains tight (cash $0.9M + restricted $6.2M) and management’s recalibrated breakeven is still pushed out to 2027 with cash-neutral only at mid-$20M revenue—consistent with the bear case rather than a clear acceleration. New wins/small tool sale are positives, but they don’t outweigh the underlying margin/guidance reality for a stock priced for turnaround.

Underlying operating metrics came in stronger than the pre-release base case (notably same-location NOI +12% and RevPAS to ~$225), and there was additional debt paydown plus asset-rotation progress. However, FY26 guidance was reaffirmed and (per the note) the market’s key risk is the going-concern/LOC language and the Aug 12 IOI expiry—neither is confirmed here—so the net reaction is roughly neutral-to-slightly positive rather than a clear beat-and-raise outcome.

This release reads largely like the already-expected financing/cash-runway and continued 2H’26 interim PoC + Q4’26 endometriosis timing. The upside is mainly the stronger-than-expected cash balance ($201.1M vs ~$190–200M expectation) and improved prolactin-occupancy modeling language, but the R&D/SG&A increases and the unchanged (not tightened) clinical timeline keep much of the “big beat” out of the quarter. Net: likely modestly positive, close to median.

Headline results came in mixed: revenue missed consensus while adjusted EBITDA exceeded the Street’s rough expectations, but management noted base business declined (−2.9%), and the EBITDA outperformance was helped by tariff refunds (one-time). Guidance was reaffirmed rather than tightened, so the market likely leaned on the weaker underlying base-sales tone and modestly reduced confidence in sustaining H2 margin requirements.

Q2 revenue and loss were roughly in line with the (low-confidence) single-source quarter expectations, while the bigger event—FY26 revenue—was reaffirmed ($72–76M) with no new evidence that the H2 ramp hurdle is being walked back. Upside came from higher gross margin guidance and some ECO/partner progress, but it’s not enough to overcome the still-steep $43–47M H2 requirement.

FY27 guidance was raised vs the stock-note’s base case risk around tax normalization: revenue and especially adjusted EPS ($6.04-$6.24) appear to land above the $5.86 consensus framing, with assisted share/retention trends continuing. With Q4 largely predetermined and the tax-bridge well telegraphed, the upside is likely incremental rather than a major repricing catalyst.

Revenue/ARR and especially EBITDA margin came in stronger than the note’s base/bear setup (ARR held up and margin improved meaningfully), while management also raised both revenue and year-end ARR. The one notable watch-out—higher purchase-subscription mix pressuring near-term gross margin—was acknowledged but offset by margin/EBITDA expansion and stronger bookings, so the print should be neutral-to-positive rather than a re-sell.

Q2 delivered a modest revenue beat and, critically, returned to positive adjusted EBITDA and improved margins above prior-year and above the ~27–29% credibility band. Guidance action was a raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA outlook (reaffirm revenue), but the key watch item—Q3 revenue deceleration—was largely expected as durable-goods comp effects; net reaction should be solid given the margin/EBITDA credibility win.

Headline revenue beat the already-low expectations, but profitability deteriorated: adjusted EBITDA was more negative, gross margin pressured by a lossful component/freight order and shipment delays. Managed IT grew only ~8% (below the note’s key >19% bull/base watch), while procurement growth came with margin drag and NewtekOne (related-party) declined.

Revenue came in above the $2.21M consensus framework, helped by a much larger ex-US license line and a telehealth/TV-driven increase in monthly packs. However, EPS remains negative with substantial ongoing cash burn, and the call sounded more like a capital reallocation plan than a clear spending-ceiling/breakeven commitment, limiting the upside reaction.

With no revenue expected, the key read-through is operating/cash burn. Cash is sufficient and runway language remains into 2028 (inline to note). However, the reported net loss expansion is dominated by the $200M Tanabe payment, and while the note flagged EPS risk from accounting treatment, the headline loss likely reinforces worst-case optics and burn/income volatility, leading to a modestly negative reaction.

Q2 revenue and underlying RNS growth came in above the already-optimistic consensus backdrop, and management improved FY adj. EBITDA loss and gross margin guidance while keeping underlying RNS growth 21–23%. The biggest overhang (IGE PMA path) was also framed as interactive/SIR-driven rather than a disapproval, reducing downside vs the note’s bear setup; with limited EPS comparability, reaction is modestly positive rather than a breakout.

Revenue, subscribers and underlying gross margin/adjusted EBITDA all beat the note’s anchored bar, but the EPS figure is unclear and the EBITDA beat/re-raise is heavily influenced by tariff refunds (explicitly one-time). Net: a constructive print with a profitability-guide upgrade, though Prime Day unit softness is a notable offset.

Underlying profitability improved (Adj. EBITDA up 19% and SG&A as % of gross profit improved; retail margins improved). However, total Q2 revenue was slightly below expected (store consolidation headwind) and—most importantly—management signaled low-single-digit softness in current-quarter same-store sales and said refinancing details are only coming in weeks (no concrete resolution). That softening/uncertainty likely offsets the EBITDA beat versus a setup that already anticipated a good peak quarter.

Q2 revenue and losses were modestly better than the (low-bar) consensus, with a clear gross margin rebound. However, management declined to provide quarterly guidance (already expected risk in the note), and the improvement was partly attributed to shipment timing and sales of previously written-down inventory—keeping the forward demand/cash-dilution narrative closer to base than bull, limiting upside.

The key driver was a guidance raise: FY26 revenue lifted to $270–310M (midpoint $290M) vs $225–300M previously and above the ~$253.5M consensus range in the note. Backlog growth and margin expansion were also supportive, while there was no highlighted execution/lifecycle downside. Revenue vs the note’s thin ~$14.2M estimate is not a meaningful differentiator given estimate dispersion and the company’s back-end-loaded model.

Headline revenue and margin improved versus the note’s range, but the EPS outcome is driven by an opaque loss line in a solvency-style print and operating liquidity worsened (higher 1H burn, declining cash, inventory build). Q3/Q4 revenue guide is broadly consistent with a mid/high base-case ramp, while cash/runway and working-capital use remain the dominant overhang.

Q2 revenue missed consensus (~13%) amid funding headwinds and elongated cycles, but margins rebounded sequentially (gross margin 49% up 1,300 bps) and full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $16–18M (i.e., no walk-back vs a guidance-tight setup). The off-ledger story is continued cash burn plus governance/transaction uncertainty, which keeps the reaction modestly negative rather than sharply positive.

Q2 revenue and bookings are both below the pre-release expectations build (low-$20s revenue, ~$25M bookings), but management reaffirmed the key $11M deferred-revenue recognition in Q3 and provided a clear DLC timing bridge. The headline narrowed loss is largely tax-driven (one-time), keeping the underlying demand signal mixed.

Quarter revenue and EPS were essentially in line with the thin-stale consensus (note’s base case). The key upside was a clear EBITDA guidance raise, but the call also introduced a formal casino strategic review and signaled potential divestiture right as casino revenue is down YoY/seq—an uncertainty that likely outweighs the guidance upgrade given the stock’s near-high positioning into the print.

Headline EPS was worse than the already-expecting loss, reflecting higher burn. While the program de-risked on dosing completion and 12-month responder rates were stronger than the FDA-aligned threshold, the call also highlighted R&D run-rate pressure (and a new moderate SAE). Guidance/timeline for the 1H 2027 interim+FDA feedback was maintained, consistent with expectations.

Q2 revenue missed consensus and EPS loss widened, with margins pressured by low manufacturing volumes. While robotic catheter revenue and supply-constrained backlog support the MAGiC ramp, the Q3/Q4 recurring revenue guide (~$7M/$8M) is not a clear upside vs what the market modeled from the pre-release note’s >$6M recurring bogey and implies a still-strained bridge quarter; overall reaction skewed neutral-to-slightly positive given microcap near-lows and some MAGiC progress already partly anticipated.

Revenue and gross margin direction largely matched the pre-released setup, and EPS improvement is modest versus the market already expecting a pre-baked headline beat. The key negative is liquidity: cash is still low ($1.2M) with only partial credit capacity, continued going-concern language, and operating cash burn in H1 worse—overhanging any margin progress. Guidance is effectively not helped (no clear improvement vs the already-difficult FY path).

Results materially beat the modeled Q2 ramp (revenue $2.1M vs modeled ~$1.7–1.9M; EPS improved vs modeled loss range) while gross margin expanded to ~75%. Guidance was reaffirmed with timing-based caveats consistent with the note, so upside is real but tempered by the ongoing 2026 timing/back-half execution risk and stock was already lifted by prior catalysts/short positioning.

Q2 beat driven by stronger revenue/EPS and traffic-led +9% comps versus the note’s expectation that the easy-lap risk was a potential comp shortfall. However, restaurant-level margin fell (25.7% vs 26.3% prior year) and management framed back-half margin headwinds (fuel surcharges/premarinated chicken) consistent with downside scenarios, with FY guidance reiterated rather than lifted—limiting upside follow-through.

The key pre-release driver (cash/liquidity and burn math) deteriorated: reported ~$5.6M cash+ST investments by July 31 vs the note’s ~$9.5–10M straight-line expectation, with a going-concern warning. Revenue/LoI-based demand items were broadly expected to be nonbinding, but the liquidity shortfall and weaker burn trajectory dominate over modest operating cost direction.

Q4 headline results beat but were constrained by supply-gating; the more important factor (Q1 FY27 guide) came in above consensus with higher-than-modeled operating margin and continued OCS/pump laser expansion. Despite a very large GAAP charge from convertible note accounting, underlying non-GAAP margins and guide point to durable ramp rather than normalization.

Results came in well above the already-demand-optimistic setup: revenue/EPS beat, but more importantly adj. EBITDA margin surged to 19.8% (well above the ~17–17.5% hurdle) and bookings hit an all-time high. FY guidance was raised to $1.02–$1.04B (above the pre-release bull/base range), and Q3 sales were guided to another record range, supporting a re-rating rather than merely a beat.

Despite roughly in-line gross margin and lower opex, both revenue and the key leading indicator (managed services bookings) came in worse than the pre-print’s base/bull expectations, and the bookings decline/delayed contracting signals weaker near-term revenue conversion than hoped for the H2 growth story.

Headline revenue largely matches the pre-release setup (DoW delay still drives y/y weakness), and the VigilAigent/ARR narrative was already the centerpiece. The downside is EPS and underlying trajectory: net loss widened to a materially worse loss than the $(0.10) consensus, gross margin contracted sharply, and management pushed cash-flow positivity out (backed away from Q4’26 and now targets profitability in 2027). Despite funding actions, the shift in near-term liquidity/earnings power drives a negative reaction.

Q2 revenue (~$3.5M) appears broadly in line with the pre-release setup’s expectations for a low-information BARDA quarter, and FY26 revenue guidance of ~$18.5M was reiterated (already a key swing factor). However, gross margin dropped sharply (31.6%), and the quarter provided no quantified early commercial pull-through; positives were strengthened by access to non-dilutive BARDA and financing that extends runway (cash $14M). Overall reaction is muted-to-slightly positive given the stock was “show me revenue/cash,” but clearance risk is already priced.

Q2 revenue ($58.4M) and adjusted OIBDA ($2.1M) were within the pre-set guidance range, and local ad strength reached $9.5M (above the $9.1M key bar). However, management paused dividend/buybacks for debt repayment and provided no Q3/FY forward guidance due to the Captivate transaction—limiting upside and keeping the market focused on the missing guide (and any future leverage/margin friction).

The release largely confirmed the pre-announced balance-sheet/GAAP dynamics (liquidity up to ~$300M; debt effectively removed via share conversion; headline loss driven by noncash warrant/derivative marks), which the note expected. However, the regulatory outcome is worse than the note’s bull/base setup: the Lower 900 MHz proposal was not included in the final direct-to-device NPRM (negative), despite management receiving only an incremental timing signal (draft NPRM submitted to interagency review) and a partnership/SpaceX letter. With the stock already priced for regulatory optionality after the Aug 10 run, the net is a modestly negative reaction.

Q4 revenue landed at the low end as pre-announced, but non-GAAP EPS and gross margin beat sharply versus the already-low expectations for the quarter. The key offset is the Q1 FY27 guide implying margin normalization (GM ~10.4%-10.8%) and AI mix timing, limiting the upside from the mid-teens/Q4 margin reset; overall reaction is neutral-to-mildly positive versus the market’s already well-known setup.

With consensus largely stale and revenue/EPS near-diagnostic for the cash-shell, the actionable items were (1) cost/run-rate credibility and (2) buyback/catalysts. Q2 showed sequential opex improvement and cash opex targeting < $2.5M/quarter (a controlled burn) plus meaningful repurchases ($3.2M) and better gross margin; guidance was only directional, but not worse. Overall this is modestly positive versus the pre-release “base/bear” setup given the buyback and expense progress.

Reaffirmed FY26 revenue guidance ($30–35M) matched the note/consensus setup, and gross margin improved sequentially, with strong drone demand and 5x scaling to 1M cells by early Sep. Offsets: GAAP/non-GAAP losses widened, and the Q2 sequential revenue decline persisted—so the reaction should be modestly positive rather than a strong re-rate.

Q2 revenue missed the midpoint on a delayed contract (expected risk), but the dominant issue is guidance: Q3 revenue was set flat at ~$5.5M (±10%), which is materially below what was required to sustain the FY consensus (implying weaker H2 than modeled). Margin improved sharply and cash rose via ATM, but the lowered cadence and pushed-out design wins outweigh these positives.

Symbest commercial revenue improved but still sits below the note’s consensus (0.4M vs $1.12M), while margin/control signals are mixed (inventory reserve and unused capacity + a very large GAAP headline loss from non-cash items). On the upside, the V012 interim hit (efficacy + infection reduction) and the November 2026 supplemental BLA/priority-review timeline are supportive, but the revenue miss and COGS reserve temper the reaction given this is a “show-me-the-units” setup.

The key guidance on ALTITUDE-AD topline remains late-2026 (the whole thesis in the note) and cash funds into early 2027 as expected, so there’s no meaningful surprise versus the scenario base case. Underlying burn improved (R&D down as trial nears completion), which is modestly positive, while missing details on powering limits offset some upside.

Revenue matched the pre-release model and EBITDA loss improved, but gross margin fell to 27% vs expected ~29% and cash dropped sharply to $10.1M (from $18.8M), keeping runway risk high despite a modest follow-on investment post-quarter. The stock had already rallied into the print, so the margin/cash deterioration outweighs the EBITDA improvement.

TRMB beat the Q2 guide on revenue and Non-GAAP EPS and raised FY guidance (revenue +$50M at the midpoint, EPS +$0.10). Underlying momentum looks solid (record organic ARR, margin expansion), though Field Systems ARR growth was guided down due to a replacement and the strategic review/possible T&L process reduces clarity near term, keeping the reaction closer to mildly positive than a breakout.

Headline Q2 revenue beat consensus and cash/launch funding outlook was reaffirmed, but EPS was distorted by a one-time $11.7M debt extinguishment loss (underlying net loss better). The notable tension vs the pre-release note is adjusted EBITDA: reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss ($5.2M) and the six-month loss narrowed vs the note’s expectation that losses would widen sharply for the commercial build; plus the debt-extinguishment charge is a negative headline. Net reaction is modestly positive given guidance reaffirmation and continued push for a potential Class 1 review, but not strongly bullish because the key implied marginal improvement (EBITDA ramp) didn’t show up.

Q2 headline revenue and EPS came in well above the thin consensus, but the pre-release note emphasized the quarter as mostly noise given Chiesi/Fiocruz shipment lumpy timing and focused on FY2026 guidance language. With no reported FY guide change in the facts provided, the print looks more like an upside quarter than a durable step-up versus expectations. Underlying support is mixed: revenue rose, but management attributed the strength largely to partner inventory management rather than clear demand acceleration.

Q2 revenue and comps landed in line, but EPS and—more importantly—adjusted operating margin materially beat due to stronger profitability. Management raised full-year adjusted operating income while narrowing revenue/comp guidance (lower top-end comp), and traffic softness persists (value-seeking customers, longer purchase cycle), limiting upside despite the guidance improvement.

While Q2 absolutes are directionally in line with the pre-release setup, the key incremental positive was a clean raise (EPS to $5.25–$5.35 and GM to 49.8–50%) that better-than-cushion indicates tariff drag is being managed and margins are improving. Underlying signals (Wrangler US wholesale flat) are not a clear beat, limiting upside in reaction despite the margin/guidance lift.

Headline revenue of ~$2M matched the amortization baseline from the note, and the EPS upside appears driven by non-cash spectrum exchange gains already highlighted as the main swing factor. The more decision-relevant items—cash, contracted proceeds, and commentary on accelerating utility conversations plus satellite optionality support—were broadly consistent with the note’s base/bull ingredients, with no clear guidance deterioration.

Reported burn (net loss $22.8M; R&D $18.7M) is broadly in line with the note’s pre-revenue framing, but the cash update is a clear reaffirmation (ended 6/30 with $519M funding to the 2029 MASH readout). Upside is mainly from added operational specificity (PERFORMA site activation pace and RESTORE enrollment/protocol amendment), which the note only loosely anticipated; downside catalysts (runway wobble) did not materialize. Stock likely reacts modestly given it was already priced around the $3 pin and near-term catalysts are still beyond this print.

Revenue missed consensus and the company cut FY26 revenue guidance to $20–23M (below the $23M low-end implied/expected), driven by delayed Water for Energy and lower utilization/mix. Despite a record $1.5M commercial pool quarter, gross margin fell sharply and underlying profitability worsened (adj. EBITDA more negative), making the setup negative for next-day reaction.

Q2 revenue and especially adjusted EPS were far below the pre-release expectations (and the miss was not rescued by any recurring margin/cost offset). While backlog surged more than expected, gross margin still came in with a ~20% handle and was pressured by Big 3 runoff and China tariffs; the adjusted earnings power deteriorated and suggests the recovery is not yet showing up in the P&L.

Revenue and the underlying commercial ramp (patient starts, prescriber depth) met or slightly beat expectations, and profitability continued to improve. However, adjusted EPS landed below the pre-print bar (notably vs the higher-consensus EPS), and management provided no new tighter guidance—on a stock that trades like a legal-outcome story—so the net reaction is modestly negative/neutral rather than a strong beat-and-raise.

Q4 landed near/at the pre-set base expectations (revenue not clearly upside; adj. EPS growth modest), but adjusted EBITDA finished at the upper end and FY27 EBITDA implies a mid-point around the note’s $2.10B hurdle. The notable upside is organic independent cases (+5.8%) supporting the forward story; the main offset is that FY27/earnings growth still looks execution-dependent while the call highlights ongoing diesel headwinds and no explicit major acceleration beyond stated ramp.

Revenue and H2 growth guidance (>50% vs H1) largely met/beat what the note framed as the bull/base range, but EPS/underlying profitability are worse than feared due to the still-present vessel charter cost drag. The prepayment/liquidity support and record 2027 revenue narrative are positives, yet the headline miss and margin sensitivity likely cap the upside into the call.

Headline Q4 EPS matches the Street and revenue is expected to clear the guided/company bar without a clear beat. The key incremental positive is stronger-than-expected demand optics (Chili’s 21 consecutive quarters plus acceleration in July/Aug) and margin improvement direction, but FY27 guidance is not clearly above the level implied in the note, so the reaction is modestly positive rather than a rerating spike.

Q4 revenue beat consensus (27% YoY to $196.3M) and adjusted operating income swung positive to $18.6M, consistent with the note’s bull/base framing. However, management did not provide quantified FY27 earnings guidance in the provided facts; the key variable (FY27 language) sounds constructive but the setup was already recognized as relatively fully valued into the print, leading to a neutral-to-modestly positive reaction.

Revenue came in about in-line vs the pre-release base ($33.4M vs ~$32.7M), but the EPS/EBITDA deterioration (net income and EBITDA both down YoY) is worse than the preview’s expectation of another profitable step ($EPS ~$0.04, EBITDA ~$1.25M). Buybacks resumed (positive), yet SLS revenue declined more than the preview’s base implied (~$10.1M vs ~$8.8M expected), while underlying profitability softened overall despite margin improvement.

Revenue ($19.3–19.4M) missed the ~$21.23M consensus and also failed the note’s key “arithmetic gate” (~$20.5M) for the FY27 $85–95M+ guide. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was higher, but Slacker’s margin was explicitly boosted by non-recurring stock-for-service/liability eliminations—so underlying profitability signal is less clean—keeping the likely reaction negative despite improved GAAP losses.

Q2 revenue ($4.9M) beat the very loose consensus anchor, but the underlying profitability was weak (gross profit only $0.37M) and the net loss slightly worsened. The key upside is the clear FY26 revenue guidance raise to ~$15M and improved cash outlook, partially offset by delays (200 kW pushed to 2027) and continued heavy dilution risk signals—overall a modestly positive, not “priced-for-perfection,” reaction.

Q1 revenue ($16.1M) and adjusted EBITDA ($1.6M) came in around the note’s realistic base, with margin contribution improving. However, EPS was more negative than the note’s small-positive/flat expectations and, critically, there was no quantified AI/LLM licensing “dollars recognized” disclosure to de-risk the FY27 guide thesis—an item the note flags as a key swing factor.

Headline P&L items (loss narrowing; no material revenue) are broadly in line with a pre-solvency compliance-focused setup. The key items versus the note are (1) equity/cash outcome supports continued listing (cash $5.4M; equity $2.7M), which is better than the note’s likely short equity case, and (2) enrollment remains slow (only 4 sites; no total enrollment), reinforcing the note’s base/bear concern about missing pacing—so the net reaction is mildly positive but not a strong upside rerate.

The call largely confirmed what the market was braced for: no meaningful revenue/EPS items and cash/runway language extends through 2027. The key incremental read-through was improved risk tone on safety for C-BEYOND (no drug-related SAEs/discontinuations) offset by cautious/forward-looking NDA timing (C-FORWARD results early Q1’27 with NDA anticipated in Q2’27, implying the earlier filing path is not nearer-term). Net reaction is modestly negative-to-neutral for a catalyst-driven name, with downside skew consistent with the pre-note.

Results beat consensus and the Q1 FY27 guide midpoint ($2.10B revenue, $1.95 EPS) is solid versus the note’s base case. However, COHR was already priced for near-bullish outcomes (+~8.8% into the print) and the note’s key risk was the DC&C acceleration/guide bar; while guidance clears it, the setup remains ‘beat-and-fade’ rather than a clear upside re-rating. No underlying margin/demand deterioration was flagged, limiting downside but also capping upside.

Q4 revenue and non-GAAP EPS beat the high end of guidance, and—critically—FY27 guidance was raised to ~mid-$5.08 EPS and ~15% revenue growth with strong product/order momentum. This improves on the note’s base case and offsets the margin headwind signal; downside would have required weaker AI conversion/orders or sub-4.80 EPS guidance, which did not occur.

Q2 fundamentals look clearly better than the note’s expectation gap for the quarter (revenue and, critically, net revenue/ASP mix and adjusted EBITDA turned strongly positive). However, the biggest overhang in the note was the lack/deferral risk around formal FY26 guidance and back-half ramp credibility; no guidance update was provided in the call facts, keeping the story from being a “beat-and-raise” rerating setup. Negative: base business/other brands were still described as slightly light (QBREXZA).
