Revenue was near the ~$14.5M ask (14.4 vs consensus) but the key underlying metric missed: adjusted EBITDA fell to ~$0.24M vs ~$0.6M expected, and management disclosed meaningful one-off retention and litigation costs that roll off later—implying the core cadence is still weak. With no numeric guidance raise and the balance sheet still drawing down (cash down to $7.7M), the print reads more like the bear case than a re-acceleration.

Q2 delivered a better-than-outlook quarter (gross margin above range; adj EPS well above the modeled ~$0.12 bar) while raising FY26 guidance by lifting the comp low end (and EBITDA/EPS ranges). Offsetting the beat, management flagged a cyclospora-related ~100bp Q3 comp headwind, so upside may be capped versus a clean beat-and-guide.

Revenue growth/acceleration and customer/hospital adoption were better than the model, but the key underwrite is liquidity: cash burn continues and net loss widened with operating expense doubling. Enrollment (223/339) is near the base-case but below the 225 “red/green” watch level, tempering upside; with going-concern dynamics already framed in the note and no guidance raise, the net reaction is modestly neutral-to-slightly positive.

SaaS guidance is reaffirmed, which is broadly in line with the note’s base case expectations. However, the underlying profitability deteriorated sharply (net loss widened, adjusted EBITDA turned materially worse) and gross margin slipped, while SaaS growth (+4.2% YoY) was well below the note’s “sanity check” for double-digit progress—raising credibility concerns for the FY26 double-digit SaaS commitment despite stable guidance language.

Despite very small reported P&L relevance, the call provided incremental reassurance: late-cycle review meeting completed, PDUFA target reaffirmed for Oct 30, and runway extended into late Q1 2027. However, the FDA did not resolve accelerated-approval eligibility (still flagged as an open issue), keeping the core binary unresolved and consistent with the pre-release setup.

Underlying commercial metrics (KOMZIFTI net product revenue above the note’s ~$9–10M bar and new starts up ~35% QoQ with prescriptions +60%) came in better than expected, supporting the bull case. However, the quarter still showed margin pressure (SG&A up materially) and cash declined, so reaction is positive but not extreme versus a stock that was already widely anticipating a launch-curve confirmation.

Revenue was largely pre-announced and therefore priced in; the key swing factors were cash/burn and margin quality. Cash came in below the note’s $10M “relief” threshold ($8.2M), while opex jumped sharply (integration/R&D), implying continued dilution/financing risk—more than offset by gross margin turning positive and reaffirmed (not raised) guidance.

Revenue and gross margin beat the note’s base case, but operating income declined and EPS was only essentially flat while cash use worsened with a sizable working-capital build. Backlog grew (positive), yet incentive comp pressure and low cash/limited revolver availability offset the margin strength, keeping the reaction near-median.

The key expectation was timing language for ELPIS-2 topline; management moved it to mid-September (database lock Aug 31), which is a negative drift versus the note’s base expectation of August/early September. Liquidity also worsened (cash $10.1M vs expected ~$11–11.5M) and losses/guidance toward needing financing into 4Q6 reinforce risk. While the auction/partnering emphasis and unchanged near-term data narrative are not a beat, the cash shortfall and slight catalyst slippage drive a negative reaction.

Revenue was far above the note’s low-to-mid teens expectation (Q2 net sales $28.5M vs ~$13M “no-acceleration”), and account growth/demand commentary is strong (73 accounts; adult mix ~95%). However, guidance was not provided (as expected) and much of EPS optics is distorted by the derivative mark-to-market—so the incremental upside may be more limited than the magnitude of the headline revenue beat, especially after the stock’s +57% run into the print.

Q2 tracked the pre-release build (revenue ~$7.3M vs ~$7.0M; core $6.5M vs ~$6.2M; SPL $0.8M matches the ~Casgevy royalty math). The main signal is constructive—SPL/royalty strength aligned—while gross margin fell to 77% and management guided mid-70s margins for H2, keeping sentiment neutral-to-slightly positive given guidance was reiterated.

The quarter beat revenue and non-GAAP EPS, and gross margin guidance was raised, but demand weakened materially (NRR fell to 90%, top-20 ARP down) and adjusted EBITDA was hit by severance. Because FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at the pre-release level (the key swing item), the print looks more like differentiation on profitability than an overturn of the H2 inflection narrative—so reaction is near-median.

The quarter looks broadly in line to slightly worse on earnings, with a customer-directed hold pushing treatment revenue into 2H while costs were incurred—consistent with the note’s “bear” framing that operating leverage won’t show up yet. However, treatment backlog growth (29% QoQ to $15.7M), the already-reported Hanford IDIQ award, and cash from the May offering reduce near-term dilution risk, limiting downside despite weaker margins.

The call delivered mixed fundamentals vs the note: same-store sales were in the expected band and restaurant margin beat modestly, but revenue and (especially) adjusted EBITDA were below the implied ~$21–22M expectation and marketing-driven spend weighed on profit. Guidance was maintained and clarified as excluding refranchising impacts, which reduces the “guidance re-base” headline risk that the note flagged; net reaction should be slightly positive but not a rally given underlying EBITDA softness and thin traffic growth proof.

The release was essentially an operational update (enrollment, LPO/timing, PMA timeline, cash/runway) with no meaningful EPS/revenue signal. Incremental operational positives—75% enrollment with all sites activated and strengthened Nefamostat market/supportive guideline and procedures research—are better than the base-case “on track” setup, while guidance/timing to PMA/top-line remains broadly consistent with the note’s expectations.

Q2 revenue landed above the ~$24.1M consensus (and within the pre-release “whisper” band), but gross margin fell to 29% and B2B shipments are only just beginning; the Gen 3 timeline remains dependent on regulatory approvals with no firm date. Guidance was reaffirmed only to become cash-flow positive exiting 2026, which the note flagged as a credibility window.

Revenue and underlying operating momentum were roughly in line with expectations from the note (continued headwinds from SREC production/performance incentives and a slower Spruce Pro ramp), while operating EBITDA was stronger (26.5M vs 24.0M modeled). The EPS improvement is heavily influenced by non-cash swap valuation moves, and the core refinancing narrative did not clear the bull threshold: SP1 is still described as preliminary with no committed term sheet, and the going-concern qualification remains—limiting upside for the equity despite cash being solid and guidance reaffirmed.

Growth accelerated and FY26 revenue guidance was raised to 14–16% vs the note’s top-of-range 10–12% expectation, while the company posted a second consecutive profitable GAAP quarter. The one remaining key risk—gross margin validation—was not clearly quantified in the provided facts (so upside is more growth/margin narrative than a fully proven margin snap), tempering the reaction.

On revenue, WATT’s ~$3.1M is essentially consistent with the note’s ~$3.47M anchor (and the market was already focused on share count and H2 ramp rather than a small beat/miss). The mix is worse than expected: gross margin fell to 19% with clear retooling/absorption cost pressures, and gross margin compression directly challenges the cleaner operating-leverage path the note was looking for. Offsetting positives are incremental diversification in customer concentration and a reaffirmed no-ATM stance, but the margin setup likely weighs more than the top-line beat.

Headline EPS/net income look strong due to the SDC divestiture gain, but underlying continuing-ops results missed the market’s framing: orders were only ~$1.2M and backlog fell to ~$3.9M (below the ~$4M floor in the note) with a key system order at risk post-bankruptcy. No meaningful capital-allocation or re-rating catalyst was added, and demand commentary remained cautious for PVT/SiC and aerospace follow-ons.

Revenue and gross margin were essentially on top of what the note already said was likely (pre-released at $5.2M; 57% GM). The main surprise bucket—GAAP EPS optics from convertible-debenture accounting—was still largely non-cash and nonrecurring, but the Q2 bookings/backlog came in slightly lighter than the note’s backlog sensitivity (backlog down to $2.1M). Overall, the print is better than “worst case” but not a meaningful upside catalyst versus expectations, keeping reaction modest.

Q2 revenue and licensing came in above what the note required (~$22.8M H1 Q2 midpoint and ~$13–14M implied licensing), with strong gross/EBITDA margin leverage. However, the print still guides to a clear step-down in 2H adj. EBITDA (to $6–$10M) and explicitly more conservative licensing assumptions, partially offsetting the upside and keeping the market cautious.

EPS/revenue are non-informative (pre-revenue burn story). The call delivered some useful pipeline/operational detail (site activation quantified to 100 by year-end; reiterated mid-2027 interim timing) but added no clear “ALPHA3 enrollment acceleration that changes the mid-2027 read” and guidance/pace was effectively maintained versus the note’s base case. Net: modestly neutral-to-slightly positive setup rather than a directional beat.

Headline EPS swung positive largely aided by tariff-related adjustments, but underlying operating direction looks better via a large gross-margin expansion and improved marketing leverage. The key negative is the dividend cut (income/liquidity narrative) and the quarter’s cash story implying a more cash-constrained posture despite the improved sales/margins.

Revenue came in roughly in-line with the (stale) consensus, but the call highlighted weaker DSP-driven demand, worsening adjusted EBITDA losses, and liquidity fell to ~$0.5M with covenant-waiver discussions ongoing. With the note emphasizing cash/maturity/refinancing as the binary, the lack of any clear positive in the lender/cash narrative points to a negative-to-mild reaction.

The reported quarter reinforced the pre-printed bear case: flipped gross margin to negative via sharply higher (grant-driven) cost of revenue and, most importantly, disclosed substantial going-concern doubt with a shortened cash runway. While product pilot progress (80% productivity gain) is positive, there was no concrete capital/financing mitigation, so the call is likely to be read as dilution risk intensifying rather than resolving.

Q2 landed at the high end of the (already-known) range, but the market’s key test—Q3 revenue ($9–10M) versus the ~$11M need to hold FY26—looks only modestly supportive rather than decisive. While smart eyewear ramp volume was reiterated/advanced (Q3 packs ~19k), management also guided negative smart-eyewear gross margin for the rest of 2026 and non-GAAP gross margin fell YoY, tempering conviction on the 2H/FY26 ramp.

Despite a still-lossy Street EPS number, the quarter showed clean underlying improvement (62.4% GM, adj. op income ~$9M) and—most importantly—FOSL raised FY26 sales and operating margin guidance and guided to positive full-year FCF, plus wholesale/traditional watch growth (12% global; 16% US). With the stock previously run up, the beat is partly expected, but the raise/FCF shift is meaningfully better than the note’s base case.

Q2 revenue and EPS beat the (already high) guidance range, and management raised FY26 broadband revenue and EPS—most importantly, it did not confirm the note’s feared 2H gross-margin deterioration; backlog also printed as a record with strong 12-month conversion and a book-to-bill well above 1.0. Balance-sheet/cash flow remained messy, but the core visibility/margin story was better than the pre-release bear setup.

Headline GAAP and NAV are strong, but they were largely predictable given the HYPE mark-to-market framing in the pre-release note. Guidance for FY26 adjusted gross profit ($5–7M) was reiterated (not raised), while the note flagged redeployment timing (idle ~300K) and a cash-flow constraint risk—Q2 showed progress (1.0M redeployed; new HAUS/house partners), but USDH/Felix monetization revenue is down and validator commissions remain small, keeping the outcome mixed vs the note’s bear-case ramp concerns.

Despite the already-highlighted restructuring risk, the operational print deteriorated further vs what the note implied (sales and adj. EBITDA both below the ~$78–82M/peak-season setup) and—most importantly—management withdrew full-year guidance and highlighted weak traffic plus elevated balance-sheet risk with low liquidity. The interchange settlement helped headline net income but is one-time and does not offset the underlying EBITDA/margin miss.

While the company modestly raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance (midpoint ~$227.5M vs $225–235M framework in the note) and reported adjusted EBITDA up QoQ YoY, underlying demand remained slightly negative (SSS -1.1%) and margins/comps deteriorated (RLM down to 17.6%, franchise margin down, commodity inflation explicitly pressured Q3). The note already flagged an approaching-flat bar and stub sensitivity, so the net outcome is near-median reaction rather than a strong relief.

Underlying profitability deteriorated sharply (adj. EBITDA down 85%, margin 1.7%) and full-year guidance was lowered with no near-term growth expectation. This is worse than what the note framed as the main uncertainty being a guidance reinstatement/clean base rather than an additional deterioration.

Revenue came in materially worse than the pre-release base/own model (orders and YoY revenue -17%), even as gross margin and adjusted EBITDA exceeded the ~$0.5M bar and wholesale/occasion categories showed traction. Guidance was reaffirmed, but the miss on the top-line growth/trend is likely to dominate near-term given the strategic-review and MVLS tail risk.

Headline results largely track the market’s low-revenue expectations and negative EPS consensus, with no provided Q4/FY guidance to force a repricing. The key swing factors are (i) margin pressure (net loss widening on higher opex) and (ii) balance-sheet/liquidity strength being only modestly offset by incremental STS contribution and reaffirmed NRC timeline—netting to a near-median outcome.

Q2 revenue was essentially inline versus the note’s $11.20M expectation, while the core focus (adj. EBITDA/quality) wasn’t materially better than what the note framed as the key test. The bigger swing is Q3 guidance, which came in higher than a standalone ~$2M+ framing would imply, but the note already emphasized that Archenia is the main driver and that cash remains a key cross-check; guidance looks supportive but not an unambiguous upside catalyst versus the base case.

Headline quarter looked strong, but the call emphasized (i) non-recurring separation cash drag in Q2 and (ii) tariff refunds won’t recur, while also flagging cost inflation that may halt the gross-margin growth streak—signals that the standalone re-rating story could stall despite flat guidance. Standalone FY revenue/EBITDA outlook was maintained, so the main surprise is margin/cash-flow risk rather than upside upside.

Revenue came in far below already-soft expectations, and the underlying loss widened with higher operating expenses—counter to the cost-control/ramp narrative in the note. Guidance/underlying IL impact was framed as minimal (inline), but the key execution risk increased: CE marking slipped to Q4 2026 (explicit negative) while margins contracted; payer discussions improved, partially offsetting. Net effect: modestly negative reaction.

Underlying revenue momentum and operating-cash-flow milestone were supportive, but EPS/EBITDA are still negative and the key check (exit-2026 run-rate and EBITDA range) was largely reiterated—rather than meaningfully upgraded beyond the note’s base/bull framing. The equity raise is a sentiment overhang. Net: modestly positive but not a high-conviction beat/raise outcome given priced-for-perfection setup and limited EPS upside.

Revenue and the key FY26 revenue guidance were reiterated and consistent with the pre-release framework (the market’s focus was the H2 backlog/contracting level). However, gross margin dropped sharply to 38% (impacted by a canceled contract and cleanup) and EBITDA remains negative, which is a meaningful quality-of-earnings strike versus what the note implicitly hoped to see. Contracting improved (>85% vs 76% previously), providing some offset.

The key thesis catalyst missed: first commercial spaceflight pushed from the expected/market narrative to Feb 2027 (vs note base case of staying on track). Liquidity/runway ended cash better than the note’s rough band and ATM cash raised were solid, but Q3 FCF guidance moved worse (−95 to −100 vs the −87 to −92 guide) with higher Q3 capex, reinforcing dilution/burn fears. Net reaction is negative despite stronger demand/payment and higher cash.

Headline confirms the key narrative items (UTEBI approval, non-dilutive royalty financing, SP001 Phase II start targeted for Q2’27, runway extended to H2’29). However, Q2 loss widened to $9.6M (worse than the pre-release modeled EPS range) and there was no disclosed unmodeled Q2 GSK milestone revenue—so the quarter is broadly as expected while the cost structure/margin deterioration is a slight offset. With the stock already priced for an event-driven call, reaction is modestly negative-to-neutral.

Reported Q2 revenue (~$34M) was slightly below the note’s derived ~$40M expectation, but margins improved (record non-GAAP GM) and operating cash flow turned to breakeven (+$0.3M). Guidance was reaffirmed with no new deterioration, which is neutral given the stock was already positioned for a cash-reversal quarter; the lack of battery-resale progress limits upside.

Headline EPS likely benefited from the large GAAP debt-restructuring gain, which the note expected as the key non-operating catalyst. Underlying EBITDA improved, but Q2 revenue remains pressured and Q3 same-station guidance is still a mid-single-digit decline, leaving the setup largely within the note’s base/bear operating frame. The net read is mildly positive on operating costs but constrained by ongoing demand/agency weakness and only “minimal” Q4 political visibility.

Revenue came in above the already pre-announced $90M+ pace (to $93.5M) with China showing no distributor inventory build, and EVO+ is tracking ahead of launch expectations—both were key risk items in the note. EPS reported profit ($0.16 diluted) is below the $0.22 consensus figure, but the note’s EPS anchor was flagged as unreliable; management also did not meaningfully change the guidance posture, keeping the reaction moderate-to-positive.

Q2 revenue of $17.8M and reaffirmed FY2026 guidance were broadly in line with the note’s low-growth / margin-critical setup. The key swing factor—gross margin expanding to 18%—landed slightly better than the note’s base-case (18–19% vs an implied risk of 18–19% with possible startup drag), which should support a modestly positive tape; however, adjusted EBITDA remained negative in Q2 and EPS is still loss-making, limiting upside.

Revenue came in slightly above the pre-release Q2 consensus, but the key solvency/risk item was not supportive: cash ended at $65.4M with funding only into September 2026 and a near-term Sep 10 $15.8M payment that would breach the liquidity covenant without additional financing/waiver. Guidance was reaffirmed (FY26 $130–150M), but without a named financing or runway extension, the print is unlikely to change the October covenant overhang versus what the note already anticipated. Sentry and FDA feedback on SVR35 as a reasonably likely surrogate are positives, yet they don’t resolve the financing timeline.

No meaningful financial surprise (pre-revenue; EPS as noise), and cash/runway commentary is broadly in line with the pre-note. The notable upside is stronger-than-anticipated clinical durability/response messaging (Clover-WM major response and 17.8-month follow-up), but it doesn’t change the binary catalyst timing as much as EMA/Phase 3 submission confirmation would.

Q4 EPS beat ($1.32 vs ~$1.25 expected) with margin up (gross margin +180 bps) and strong customer momentum. Most importantly, FY27 EPS guided to $7.80–$7.90 (midpoint $7.85) which is above both consensus (~$7.45–$7.50) and the Amplify-style bull threshold, while FY27 revenue and operating margin are also constructive—an upside surprise for a stock previously priced for perfection.

Revenue of $1.8M is essentially in the middle of the pre-release base case (about meet guidance / miss consensus framing) while management reaffirmed CY2026 $8M and CY2027 $16–18M. The key negative vs the note is Gen 2 timing shifting further to Q4 (vs the note’s H2 expectation), while positives include improved gross margin (third consecutive positive gross profit) and a larger commercial pipeline (GPO wins).

Headline revenue of $11.4M missed the ~$12.2M consensus implied in the note and the loss widened to -$0.35. Revenue and OEM/engineering monetization look weaker than the note’s “pivot must show up in Q2” setup (revenue -14% YoY to $1.1M vs $1.50M expected; engineering services $0.2M vs implied $0.35–0.45M).
